9.6.1. qnav.input.config

9.6.1.1. config.py

summary:

Obtains primary simulation components from configuration file. This module is used for initialising and obtaining the main components used in simulations and for logging details to the console.

author:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First full implemented version.

qnav.input.config.get_configuration(config_file: Path = None) → ConfigHandler[source]

Initialises and returns a qnav.input.config.ConfigHandler instance using the contents of the given file. On succession, the file’s variables, along with those in any sub-configurations, will be parsed and loaded. If not file is given, a default settings file will be used.

Parameters:

config_file (Path) – A path for a configuration (.ini) file to use.

Returns:

An initialised ConfigHandler instance.

Return type:

ConfigHandler

qnav.input.config.get_trajectory(config: ConfigHandler) → Trajectory[source]

Extracts values and produces ground truth trajectories. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and uses them to generate a trajectory. On succession, this is return ready for use in a simulation.

Parameters:

config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

Returns:

The trajectory ready for use in a simulation.

Return type:

Trajectory

qnav.input.config.get_estimation(config: ConfigHandler, trajectory: Trajectory) → EstimatedState[source]

Extracts values and produces the initial estimation state. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and uses them to initialise the starting estimation information. This uses the first record from the previously generated trajectory and induces any requested errors. On succession, an initial estimated state is return.

Parameters:

  • config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

  • trajectory (Trajectory) – The trajectory to be used during the simulation. Required to obtain the true state at the first time step.

Returns:

The initial estimated state to use in the simulation.

Return type:

EstimatedState

qnav.input.config.get_platform_hardware(config: ConfigHandler, estimated_state: EstimatedState) → list[SensorFusion][source]

Extracts values and produces the virtual platform hardware instances. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and uses them initialize and return the requested Sensor-Fusion instance to use during the simulation. On succession, a list of SensorFusion classes to use in a simulation are returned.

Parameters:

  • config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

  • estimated_state (EstimatedState) – The initial estimates before start of simulation. Required as some fusion methods need an initial estimate to start with.

Returns:

The list of SensorFusion instances to use in a simulation.

Return type:

list[SensorFusion]

qnav.input.config.get_platform_clock(config: ConfigHandler) → Clock[source]

Extracts values and produces a virtual platform clock instances. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and uses them to initialise and return the platform clock to use.

Parameters:

config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

Returns:

The Clock instance to use in a simulation.

Return type:

Clock

qnav.input.config.get_collector(config: ConfigHandler) → ResultsCapture[source]

Extracts values and produces the results collection instance to use. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and uses them initialise and return a results collection instance, responsible for filtering and collecting simulation results.

Parameters:

config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

Returns:

The ResultsCapture instance to use in a simulation.

Return type:

ResultsCapture

qnav.input.config.get_displayer(config: ConfigHandler) → Display[source]

Extracts values and produces the displaying instance to use. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and uses them initialise and return a display instance, responsible for feeding back real-time information about the simulation. Can also be used for stopping the simulation prematurely when criteria is met.

Parameters:

config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

Returns:

The Display instance to use in a simulation.

Return type:

Display

qnav.input.config.get_results_settings(config: ConfigHandler) → dict[source]

Extracts values and produces the results generation settings. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and uses them to define how results will be gathered after the simulation and exported.

Parameters:

config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

Returns:

A dictionary containing settings for exporting results.

Return type:

dict

qnav.input.config.get_figure_settings(config: ConfigHandler) → dict[source]

Extracts values to use for results figure and report generation. When called, this function reads the required variables from the given configuration and returns them in a dictionary. These can then be used later for generating the relevant after-simulation graphics and report results.

Parameters:

config (ConfigHandler) – The ConfigHandler instance to use for simulation settings.

Returns:

Dictionary containing figure generation settings.

Return type:

dict

qnav.input.config.print_banner(text: str = None)[source]

Used to print formatted heading in the output console. Simply used to group list points together cleanly.

Parameters:

text (str) – (Optional) The text to include in the heading. If not provided a dividing line will be used.

qnav.input.config.print_line(field: str, value: any)[source]

Used to print formated lines in the output console. Simply used to produce clean uniformly spaced list points.

Parameters:

  • field (str) – The text to place on the left-hand side.

  • value (any) – The value to place on the right-hand side.
